note: Rockefeller Center: five hero kits (runs/rockefeller-center: 30 Rock, the plaza and Channel Gardens, Radio City, the International Building with Atlas and the Fifth Avenue pair, St Patrick's Cathedral), each module on its footprint or open-ground box at its own ground level; the metered Haiku fill (bin/fill.mjs) on the other blocks.
common: Scale: 0.9 blocks per metre (a storey is about 3.5 blocks). For a public catalog for a Minecraft 1.21.1 server: only blocks that exist in 1.21.1 (no pale oak, no "iron_chain" (it is "chain" in 1.21.1), nothing 1.21.4+). These are real buildings of Rockefeller Center in Midtown Manhattan, New York, for a hero AERIAL render at golden hour and dusk: the camera looks down from high over Fifth Avenue, so ROOFS, setbacks and the tops of the buildings matter as much as the street fronts. Placement code sets each module on its real footprint exactly as it stands (no turning), so build each IN ITS SITE ORIENTATION, as in the maps: the Manhattan grid is square to the axes; uptown (north) is low z, downtown (south) high z; Fifth Avenue is east (high x), Sixth Avenue (Avenue of the Americas) west (low x); the cross streets (48th, 49th, 50th, 51st Streets) run along x. The ground is nearly flat: y 0 of each plot is the lowest ground under it and the GROUND map gives the ground above y 0 per cell. Build only on the footprint cells (#). Exterior only: no interiors beyond what shows through glass (lit lobbies, shop windows). No villagers. Nothing may leave its plot or exceed its stated height. Make it read at dusk: warm light in a scattering of office windows (not all), lit lobbies and shopfronts at street level, floodlit crowns and signs where the real building has them; light every roof and terrace so no mob spawns.
closing: Use the photograph only as inspiration for character and colour; the maps and dimensions above are exact.

kits.intro: 30 Rockefeller Plaza (the Comcast Building; the RCA Building of 1933, the GE Building 1988-2015), Raymond Hood and the Associated Architects: the 70-storey Art Deco slab at the heart of Rockefeller Center and the hero of the render. It must read, at a glance, as THIS tower: a thin, sheer, pale limestone slab, narrow end to the plaza (east), broad flanks north and south that step back in a cascade of setbacks, every face ribbed by continuous vertical limestone piers with dark recessed window strips between them, so it reads as a bundle of vertical lines soaring to a flat crown.

plots.label: 30 ROCKEFELLER PLAZA AND ITS SIXTH AVENUE WING
plots.text: Follow the ROOF HEIGHT map exactly: it is the real massing. THE TOWER is the tall slab in the east part of the footprint (its narrow EAST face on Rockefeller Plaza, at the footprint's high-x edge, faces the sunken plaza): the east and west faces rise sheer; the long NORTH and SOUTH flanks step back in many narrow setbacks (each a ledge 1-3 blocks deep, crowned with stair/slab copings), so from the air the slab narrows in tiers toward its top. Walls: pale buff Indiana limestone (smooth_sandstone, sandstone, end_stone_bricks or white_terracotta in a consistent light buff) as continuous vertical PIERS 1 block wide, proud of the wall, with 1-block recessed vertical window strips between them (dark: gray or black stained glass panes, with dark gray_terracotta or polished deepslate spandrels between storeys), so every face is fluted with vertical lines top to bottom; the corners are solid limestone. THE CROWN: the top three tiers are the Top of the Rock observation decks: open terraces with glass-pane parapets, the topmost a narrow flat roof with a low mechanical penthouse and a slim mast; around the crown a band of big illuminated red letters (the GE-era red-lit sign: red concrete or red stained glass over glowstone/shroomlight) on the north and south faces near the top, and the crown floodlit warm white (light blocks/shroomlights hidden in the setback ledges so the upper faces glow). THE ENTRANCE: at the base of the east face on Rockefeller Plaza, the great entrance: three tall portals under Lee Lawrie's WISDOM relief, a large polychrome-and-gold Art Deco panel over the doors (a bearded figure with dividers over gold rays and a glass block screen: gold blocks, yellow and light blue terracotta, glass) with the inscription band; lit lobby glass below. THE SIXTH AVENUE WING (the west, lower part of the footprint, about 16 storeys, as the roof map shows) is the same limestone and vertical-pier language, its flat roofs with low parapets and a few planted roof gardens, entrances and lit shopfronts on Sixth Avenue (the west face) and on 49th and 50th Streets (the south and north faces). Street level all round: tall shop windows lit warm, bronze/dark framing, flags over the entrances.

kits.intro: The Lower Plaza of Rockefeller Center with its skating rink and Paul Manship's gilded PROMETHEUS (1934), the ring of flags around it, and the Channel Gardens that run up to Fifth Avenue between La Maison Francaise and the British Empire Building: the open heart of the complex, seen from above right in front of 30 Rock. These are LANDSCAPE modules on the real ground.

plots.label: ROCKEFELLER PLAZA (THE STREET) AND THE SUNKEN LOWER PLAZA
plots.text: VERTICAL DATUM: y 0 is the rink floor's level (the lowest ground in the box); the GROUND map gives the real levels: street level around the edge at about y 4-5, the sunken plaza about 4-5 blocks lower. This module replaces EVERYTHING in its box, so rebuild the ground of every column: solid stone from y 0 up to the mapped ground with the surface at that height; keep the outermost 2 blocks of every edge at the mapped heights so it meets the streets around it. From west to east: x 0..18 is ROCKEFELLER PLAZA, the private street along the foot of 30 Rock (the tower stands just west of this box): a granite-paved street (gray_concrete road with smooth_stone or polished andesite pavers, a sidewalk on each side, a few street lamps). East of it, the SUNKEN LOWER PLAZA, about 29 wide (x 20..48) and 34 long (z 10..43), a rectangular well 4-5 blocks deep: its floor the ICE RINK (ice or packed ice, a white rim) filling most of it; at its WEST end, against the west wall, PROMETHEUS: a large gilded figure (gold blocks, raw gold / yellow terracotta for modelling, about 6 blocks long, flying horizontally, arm raised holding fire) over a ring of gold, rising from a fountain basin with water jets against a tall dark granite wall (polished blackstone / deepslate tiles) carved with the zodiac ring and an inscription; the rink's long north and south sides bordered by the sunken restaurants' glass fronts under the plaza edge (lit warm, umbrellas); stepped granite edges. AROUND THE WELL at street level: the promenade, paved in pale granite, with the famous FLAGS: a continuous ring of tall white flagpoles (end rods or white fences, 7-8 tall) every 2 blocks on all four sides of the well, each flying a coloured flag (banners or wool, 2x1, all colours, mixed like the nations' flags); low granite parapets with railings at the well's edge; on the EAST side the head of the Channel Gardens: broad granite steps down into the plaza (the Channel Gardens' axis meets the plaza at the middle of the east edge, z about 19..34), flanked by planters. Light it all (lanterns on the parapets, light under the restaurant awnings, the rink lit).

plots.label: THE CHANNEL GARDENS
plots.text: The pedestrian promenade between La Maison Francaise (just south of this box) and the British Empire Building (just north), sloping gently DOWN from Fifth Avenue (east, high x) to the plaza (west, low x): rebuild the ground of every column as in plot 0 (solid from y 0 up to the mapped ground, the surface there; keep the outermost 2 blocks of every edge at the mapped heights). Down the centre a line of SIX long rectangular GRANITE POOLS (each about 6-7 long and 3-4 wide, raised granite rims of polished andesite/polished blackstone slabs, water inside, a small bronze fountain jet at each one's end), separated by short cross walks; along both sides of the pools long raised PLANTERS full of seasonal flowers and clipped shrubs (azalea, flowering azalea, leaves, allium, tulips of several colours, peonies, roses), with granite curbs and benches; wide granite-paved walks along each side next to the buildings. At the east end the opening onto Fifth Avenue, at the west end the head of the steps down to the Lower Plaza. Lamps along the walks.

kits.intro: Radio City Music Hall (1932) and its block on Sixth Avenue, between 50th and 51st Streets: the Art Deco theatre with the most famous marquee in America, and the tower it shares the corner with. It must read, at a glance, as Radio City: the long neon MARQUEE wrapping the corner of Sixth Avenue and 50th Street in bands of red and blue neon, and the tall vertical RADIO CITY blade sign rising over the corner.

plots.label: 1270 AVENUE OF THE AMERICAS AND THE RADIO CITY CORNER
plots.text: A 31-storey Art Deco office tower in pale buff limestone, the same language as the rest of Rockefeller Center (continuous vertical limestone piers with dark recessed window strips, setbacks as the ROOF HEIGHT map shows, flat roofs with parapets). Its WEST face is on Sixth Avenue (low x) and its south-west corner (low x, high z) is THE CORNER OF SIXTH AVENUE AND 50TH STREET: the Music Hall's grand entrance. There the MARQUEE: a deep horizontal canopy band, 3-4 blocks tall, running along the whole Sixth Avenue face and around the corner along the 50th Street face (the south face, high z), with three stripes of neon: red lettering "RADIO CITY" (red concrete / red stained glass over glowstone or shroomlight, sea lanterns), a deep blue band (blue concrete/blue stained glass over light) lettered "MUSIC HALL", and gold/white bulb lines (glowstone, sea lanterns, end rods); the soffit underneath lit bright over the glazed doors. Rising from the marquee at the corner, the VERTICAL SIGN: a tall narrow blade (2 thick, about 18-22 tall) sticking out from the corner, with "RADIO CITY" in stacked red neon letters on a blue and silver face, outlined in light. Over the 50th Street entrances, a few storeys up, the round enamel plaques and tall narrow windows.

plots.label: RADIO CITY MUSIC HALL (THE AUDITORIUM)
plots.text: The theatre's great hidden auditorium: a long low block in pale buff limestone (about 9 storeys tall at most, per the ROOF HEIGHT map), its roof a broad flat or very gently curved deck (gray and light gray concrete, rooftop vents and skylights, low parapets), the rear stage house a little higher. On the 50th Street face (south, high z) the stage door and the long run of the marquee continuing from the corner (red and blue neon bands, as on plot 0), the famous Art Deco roundels (the round enamel plaques of Dance, Drama and Song: large circular reliefs of colourful terracotta) set into the limestone above the marquee; tall bronze-framed windows.

plots.label: THE BLOCK'S EAST END (TOWARD ROCKEFELLER PLAZA)
plots.text: A Rockefeller Center office building in pale buff limestone with continuous vertical piers and dark recessed window strips, about 18 storeys, setbacks as the ROOF HEIGHT map shows, flat roofs with parapets and small roof gardens; lit shopfronts and entrances along 50th Street (south) and 51st Street (north) and on Rockefeller Plaza (east, high x).

kits.intro: The Fifth Avenue front of Rockefeller Center: the International Building (1935) with Lee Lawrie's bronze ATLAS in its forecourt, and the two low six-storey buildings that flank the Channel Gardens, La Maison Francaise and the British Empire Building (1933). Seen from the air from over Fifth Avenue, it is the foreground of the hero view.

plots.label: THE INTERNATIONAL BUILDING, ITS FIFTH AVENUE WINGS AND ATLAS
plots.text: The 41-storey International Building: a pale buff limestone tower set back from Fifth Avenue (follow the ROOF HEIGHT map: the tall slab stands back in the block, the six-storey wings along Fifth Avenue in front of it), with continuous vertical limestone piers and dark recessed window strips, the slab narrowing in setbacks, a flat crown with a low penthouse, floodlit. ON FIFTH AVENUE (the east face, high x): two six-storey limestone wings (the Palazzo d'Italia to the south and International Building North to the north) with roof gardens on their flat roofs (grass, hedges, small trees, paths), and between them the tall recessed ENTRANCE FORECOURT of the International Building, framed by a monumental limestone portal; in the forecourt, on the axis of the entrance and facing Fifth Avenue (east), ATLAS: a huge bronze figure (about 11-13 blocks tall on a granite plinth) shouldering the open celestial sphere: a big armillary sphere of thin bronze rings (copper blocks, cut copper, waxed weathered copper, or chains/iron bars in dark bronze tones: a sphere about 9 across of crossing rings with a central axis), the figure in dark bronze (copper, exposed/weathered copper, brown terracotta) between two tall granite pylons; lit from below. Over the entrance doors, gilded Art Deco relief panels. Lit shopfronts along 50th and 51st Streets (south and north faces) and Fifth Avenue; the lobby glowing behind tall glass.

plots.label: THE BRITISH EMPIRE BUILDING (NORTH OF THE CHANNEL GARDENS)
plots.text: A six-storey pale buff limestone building, long along x, its narrow EAST end on Fifth Avenue (high x), its south face on the Channel Gardens (high z): vertical limestone piers with dark recessed window strips, a deeper setback top storey, a flat roof with a ROOF GARDEN (lawns, hedges, flower beds, small trees, gravel paths) seen from above. Over the Fifth Avenue entrance a gilded bronze relief panel (gold blocks and yellow terracotta in an Art Deco pattern) above tall bronze-framed doors with a coat of arms; lit shop windows along the Channel Gardens and the street.

plots.label: LA MAISON FRANCAISE (SOUTH OF THE CHANNEL GARDENS)
plots.text: The twin of the British Empire Building: a six-storey pale buff limestone building, long along x, its narrow EAST end on Fifth Avenue (high x), its NORTH face on the Channel Gardens (low z): vertical limestone piers with dark recessed window strips, a setback top storey, a flat roof with a ROOF GARDEN (lawns, hedges, flower beds, small trees, paths). Over the Fifth Avenue entrance a gilded bronze relief panel (gold and yellow terracotta Art Deco figures) above bronze-framed doors; lit shop windows along the Channel Gardens and the street.

kits.intro: St Patrick's Cathedral (James Renwick Jr., 1878, spires 1888), the Roman Catholic cathedral of New York, on Fifth Avenue across from Rockefeller Center between 50th and 51st Streets: a white marble Gothic Revival cathedral among the towers. It must read, at a glance, as THIS cathedral, especially from the air: a pale white-grey marble cross-shaped church, its WEST FRONT on Fifth Avenue with TWIN OPENWORK SPIRES and the great ROSE WINDOW between them, a long steep nave roof with pinnacles and flying buttresses, transepts, and the Lady Chapel at the east end.

plots.label: THE CATHEDRAL
plots.text: A Latin cross: the long NAVE along x from the west front (Fifth Avenue, LOW x, the footprint's west edge) to the east, the TRANSEPTS crossing it north-south about the middle (their ends on 50th Street to the south, high z, and 51st Street to the north, low z), the choir and apse beyond, and at the far EAST end the lower LADY CHAPEL (follow the FOOTPRINT and ROOF HEIGHT maps). Walls of white-grey marble (calcite, diorite, polished diorite, smooth quartz, white concrete, in a soft pale grey-white mix, not pure white) with tall pointed-arch stained-glass windows between buttresses (glass: purple, blue, red, yellow stained glass panes in pointed lancets, LIT FROM WITHIN so they glow at dusk), pinnacles (end rods, walls, pointed dripstone) topping every buttress, FLYING BUTTRESSES arching over the side aisles to the clerestory, a pierced parapet. ROOFS: a steep pitched roof over nave, transepts and choir (stairs at 45 degrees or steeper, dark grey-green slate: deepslate tiles, cobbled deepslate or dark prismarine, with a thin copper-green ridge), a small fleche at the crossing. THE WEST FRONT on Fifth Avenue: two square towers rising into TWIN OPENWORK GOTHIC SPIRES, each tower about 9 x 9 blocks, its belfry with tall louvred openings, then an octagonal pierced spire tapering to a point and a cross at about y 90 (white marble with lace-like tracery: walls, fences, slabs alternating with open gaps), crocketed edges; between the towers the tall central gable over the great bronze doors (three deep pointed portals with layered arches), and above them the great ROSE WINDOW (a round wheel window about 9 across of coloured glass in stone tracery, lit from within). Wide steps down to the Fifth Avenue sidewalk, lamps. NOTE on the maps: the lidar missed much of the cathedral's dark roof (cells reading 1-2 inside the footprint are gaps, not courtyards): the nave, transepts, choir and Lady Chapel are all roofed; the 33-41 cells show the real eaves and ridge heights.

plots.label: THE ARCHBISHOP'S RESIDENCE (MADISON AVENUE AND 51ST STREET)
plots.text: A three-storey Gothic Revival house in the same pale grey marble, steep slate roof with gables and chimneys, pointed and square-headed windows lit warm, a small walled garden to the cathedral side.

plots.label: THE RECTORY (MADISON AVENUE AND 50TH STREET)
plots.text: A three-storey Gothic Revival house, the twin of the Archbishop's residence: pale grey marble, steep slate roof with gables and chimneys, lit windows, a small garden.
